name.text: Calculating probabilities for a uniformly distributed waiting time

questiontext.text:
Achieng' arrives at a matatu stop at a random time. From past observation, the time she waits for the next matatu is uniformly distributed between 0 and {@b@} minutes. Let \(X\) be the waiting time in minutes.

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution:

Part a: The PDF Height
For a uniform distribution \(U(a, b)\), the probability density function forms a rectangle with a total area of 1. The total width of the distribution is \(b - a = {@b@} - 0 = {@b@}\).

To ensure the area equals 1, the height must be the reciprocal of the width:

\( \displaystyle f(x) = \frac{1}{b - a} = \frac{1}{{@b@}} \)

\( \displaystyle \boxed{ f(x) = {@ta1@} } \)

Part b: Interval Probability
The probability of a continuous variable falling within an interval is the area of the rectangle over that specific interval:

\( \displaystyle P(c \le X \le d) = \frac{d - c}{b - a} \)

\( \displaystyle P({@c@} \le X \le {@d@}) = \frac{{@d@} - {@c@}}{{@b@}} = \frac{{@d_minus_c@}}{{@b@}} \)

\( \displaystyle \boxed{ P({@c@} \le X \le {@d@}) = {@ta2@} } \)

Part c: Exact Value Probability
For any continuous random variable, the probability of obtaining one single, exact precise moment is always zero, because there is no "width" or area under a single point on a curve.

\( \displaystyle \boxed{ P(X = {@exact_val@}) = 0 } \)

questiondescription.text:
This question is based on the discovery activity Waiting for a Matatu and the example Basic Uniform Probabilities in the section Continuous Probability I of the CBC Grade 11 Mathematics textbook (INNODEMS).

Continuous Probability (Uniform Distribution)

truefeedback.text: Correct. The height of a uniform PDF is always \(1\) divided by the total width of the distribution.

falsefeedback.text: Incorrect. Calculate the total width of the distribution, and then find its reciprocal to get the height \(f(x)\).

truefeedback.text: Excellent. You correctly calculated the proportional area for the specified time interval.

falsefeedback.text: Incorrect. Find the width of the target interval (\({@d@} - {@c@}\)) and divide it by the total width of the entire distribution (\({@b@}\)).

truefeedback.text: Correct. Because time is a continuous variable, the probability of hitting one exact, infinitely precise moment is always zero.

truefeedback.text: You entered the value of the PDF height \(f(x)\). Remember, probability is measured by area under the curve. A single exact point has a width of 0, so its area is also 0.

falsefeedback.text: Incorrect. Think about how probability is measured for continuous variables (area under the curve). Does a single, exact number have any width or area?
